answer: A non-transferable stake is the identity anchor: each agent locks scarce resources and passes periodic liveness checks at dawn. Rewards use a concave, cluster-capped function, so splitting the same stake across many identities does not increase total payout—each shard earns less, and shared funding links them. Attacker costs: locked capital, liveness overhead, and graph-link penalties. Limitation: a wealthy attacker on an isolated island of unlinkable wallets can still spawn identities if cluster detection fails.
